rows.english: And so I have accumulated some small amount of virtue from these deeds: the bowing, the offerings, the confession, rejoicing, urging, and begging. I dedicate all of them to enlightenment. The seven parts then are (1) bowing to the Lama; (2) making offerings to her or to him; (3) confessing our negative deeds; (4) rejoicing in the good deeds of others and ourselves; (5) urging the Lama to teach; (6) begging them to stay with us; and (7) dedicating the good karma of all of these to enlightenment.  For the mandala, you can use "Here is the great earth" (Sashi pukyi), but be sure to see the entire globe.]

rows.english: It occurred to our Lord that he should circle Her to the left, and throw himself down at her feet, as the rules of the Mother Tantra prescribe. rows.acip: ,'ON KYANG THUB PA'I MKHYEN BRTZE NUS PA LA, ,SGRIB THOGS MI MNGA' PHONGS PA'I GNYEN GCIG CES, ,BDEN PA GSUNG BA'I BKA' YI 'THOR 'THUNG GIS, ,STON DANG BRAL BA'I TSA GDUNG CUNG ZAD BSAL,
rows.wylie: 'on kyang thub pa'i mkhyen brtse nus pa la, ,sgrib thogs mi mnga' phongs pa'i gnyen gcig ces, ,bden pa gsung ba'i bka' yi 'thor 'thung gis, ,ston dang bral ba'i tsha gdung cung zad bsal
rows.english: The pain of it burns us, the pain of being apart from you; but then we know that nothing can hinder the knowledge and love and power of the Able Ones; and some little part of the fire is cooled by sacred water: the truth of the words you once left for us-- "I will always be the one friend for those who have nothing."

rows.wylie: srid pa'i rtse mo nas bzung dmyal ba'i bar, ,kun la 'dod dgur dbang byed rgyal po lnga'i, ,snang tshul dran tshe cung zad yid skyo bas, ,blo bzang chos kyi rgyal mtshan zhes byas smras, ,zhes gsungs
rows.english: This then is written by Lobsang Chukyi Gyeltsen, in a moment of sadness thinking about the fate of the five kings who had their power over all the beautiful things from the level called The Peak to the lowest of the hells. [Translator's note: The "five kings" seem to be His Holiness' once-powerful organs of sense. "The Peak" is a name for the final level of the formless realm, which is thus the highest possible level we can reach within the cycle of pain.]

rows.wylie: bdag kyang deng nas skye ba thams cad du, ,lha sogs 'gro ba ma lus dgrar langs te, ,srog dang 'tsho ba yang yang phral gyur kyang , ,cung zad sdang dang khro bar ma gyur cig
rows.english: As for myself, I make here another prayer too. Suppose it happens that every person In this entire world--and I'm thinking here Of the pleasure beings and the others too-- Suddenly rises against me as their enemy, And tears away from me my very life, Or all the things I need to live. And suppose it continues on like that From this very moment all the way Through all the lives I have left to live. Well I pray that even then I may never Feel for them the slightest dislike, Or any thoughts of anger at all.

rows.acip: MA RANG SROG LA BABS PA LTA BU'I SDUG BSNGAL BYUNG BA LAS, BDAG CUNG ZAD NA PA LA SDUG BSNGAL CHE BAR BYAS, SDIG SDUG GTAM NGAN RANG SROG LA'ANG MA BLTAS PAR SHA THANG THANG DU BSGRUBS PA'I ZAS NOR THAMS CAD BDAG LA BRTZE BAS PHOG ,
rows.wylie: ma rang srog la babs pa lta bu'i sdug bsngal byung ba las, bdag cung zad na pa la sdug bsngal che bar byas, sdig sdug gtam ngan rang srog la'ang ma bltas par sha thang thang du bsgrubs pa'i zas nor thams cad bdag la brtse bas phog
rows.english: If it looked as though I might be falling even the least bit ill, this hurt my mother even more than something that might threaten her very life.  She went about obtaining, and then giving over for me, whatever money it took to assure that I would grow up healthy and strong.  And she did whatever she had to to get the money--even if it was immoral, or it physically hurt her, or damaged her reputation, or even endangered her own life.

rows.wylie: ma nam byas pa'i tshe, phan pa dang bde ba tshad med pa bsgrubs, gnod pa dang sdug bsngal tshad med pa las bskyabs, khyad par bdag gis 'di med na cung zad kyang sdod mi tshugs pa dang , 'dis kyang bdag med na cung zad kyang sdod mi tshugs pa lta bu'i yid gcugs pa bgrang las 'das pa byas
rows.english: �And during each of those lives as my mother, they worked to acquire for me unlimited forms of help and happiness.  They protected me from unlimited forms of harm and suffering. rows.english: It happened one day In a moment of mental clarity-- I was thinking a bit On the essence of all the teachings I'd heard, And the thought Made my think of all the kindness That my Lama Had ever paid to me. rows.english: And so I have accumulated some small amount of virtue from these deeds: the bowing, the offerings, the confession, rejoicing, urging, and begging. rows.english: Subtle dullness is where you still have brightness and clarity, but where you have slipped a bit from a tight hold as you lock on to the object.  The antidotes for both of these are to turn you mind to the high qualities of the Three Jewels; or to place your mind in some shining place; or to carry out the special instructions for mixing both inner winds and the mind with empty space. [Translator's note: These slightly cryptic instructions are clarified as follows in the commentary to The Path of Bliss by Master Ngulchu Dharma Bhadra (1772-1851) entitled The Treasure House of Precious Jewels (ACIP digital text S6419):

rows.english: Subtle agitation is where you are unable to keep your mind immobile on the object--it flies slightly off.  The antidote for this is to return the object to the mind and apply awareness, then continue in the meditation.

rows.acip: DES NA RANG NYAMS LA DPAGS TE RIG PA 'PHANG 'DI TZAM ZHIG BSTOD NA RGOD PA SKYE BAR 'DUG SNYAM PA LAS CUNG ZAD GLOD, 'DI TZAM DU BZHAG NA BYING BA SKYE BAR 'DUG SNYAM PA LAS CUNG ZAD 'PHAR BSTOD NA RAN PAR 'GYUR BAS,
rows.wylie: des na rang nyams la dpags te rig pa 'phang 'di tsam zhig bstod na rgod pa skye bar 'dug snyam pa las cung zad glod, 'di tsam du bzhag na bying ba skye bar 'dug snyam pa las cung zad 'phar bstod na ran par 'gyur bas
rows.english: And so you have to develop the ability to judge where you are: "If I stimulate my frame of mind to this point, I tend to get agitation "--and then you loosen up a touch.  "But if I just let my mind slack to this extent, I tend to get dullness "--and then you stimulate the mind, raise it a bit, just far enough.

rows.english: Within the walls Appears a letter bhrum And from if comes A yellow disk of command; It blazes in flame And turns to the right. It has a hub and ten spokes Hovering inside the hub And just above the spokes Are seats, each one made of A multicolored lotus, And disks of the moon and sun. Above the middle seat appear a letter hung From which I then transform.

rows.english: In the center of the crystal palace is a letter yam, And from it comes a disk of wind Colored black with a little red. Atop this comes ah, the first of the letters And from it a disk of the moon. As a bubble rising out of water A golden dhih appears In the center of the moon, And from it comes a sword Marked in the middle with dhih.

rows.acip: 'DIR 'BAD PA CHEN POS MA BSGOMS KYANG SKYE BA BDUN NA DNGOS GRUB 'GRUB PA DANG DE YANG RNAL 'BYOR CUNG ZAD SGOM PA DANG DAM TSIG DANG SDOM PA DAG PAS 'GRUB KYI DAM TSIG NYAMS NA DNGOS GRUB 'GRUB PA LTA ZHOG NGAN 'GROR 'GRO BAS BDE 'GRO YANG RNYED DKA'O ZHES GSUNGS SO,
rows.wylie: 'dir 'bad pa chen pos ma bsgoms kyang skye ba bdun na dngos grub 'grub pa dang de yang rnal 'byor cung zad sgom pa dang dam tshig dang sdom pa dag pas 'grub kyi dam tshig nyams na dngos grub 'grub pa lta zhog ngan 'gror 'gro bas bde 'gro yang rnyed dka'o zhes gsungs so
rows.english: With these vows, one will achieve the final goal within seven lifetimes--even if you make no great efforts in the other practices.  When the scriptures say this though what they mean is that a person will reach the final goal if they keep up a minimum level of deep practice, and if they keep their pledges and vows pure.  But if we fail in this pledges, the scriptures are also saying, then not only is there no question of achieving the final goal; we will instead pass to the realms of misery, and just staying in a higher birth then would be highly unlikely.

rows.acip: 'DI LA LAM RGYUD LA SKYE BA'I GNAS SKABS KYI SGO NAS LAS DANG PO PA DANG , YE SHES CUNG ZAD 'BAB PA DANG , YE SHES LA CUNG ZAD DBANG THOB PA DANG YE SHES LA YANG DAG PAR DBANG THOB PA'I GANG ZAG STE BZHIR PHYE NAS, DE DAG GIS JI TZAM ZHIG DANG JI LTAR SGOM PA'I RNAM DBYE GSUNGS PA RNAMS SHES DGOS SO,,
rows.wylie: 'di la lam rgyud la skye ba'i gnas skabs kyi sgo nas las dang po pa dang , ye shes cung zad 'bab pa dang , ye shes la cung zad dbang thob pa dang ye shes la yang dag par dbang thob pa'i gang zag ste bzhir phye nas, de dag gis ji tsam zhig dang ji ltar sgom pa'i rnam dbye gsungs pa rnams shes dgos so
rows.english: The answer to your question involves a division into practitioners of four different levels, according to the degree to which the path has grown within their hearts: (1) those who are just beginners; (2) those upon whom a small measure of wisdom has descended; (3) those who have gained some small degree of control over wisdom; and (4) those who have gained total control over wisdom.  You must acquaint yourself then with the different descriptions from the scriptures on how far each one goes in the practice, and how they practice it.

rows.acip: YE SHES CUNG ZAD BABS PA NI, GZHAL YAS KHANG DANG DE LA BKOD PA'I LHA RAGS PA RNAMS NAM GSAL BTAB NA YAN LAG NYING LAG THAMS CAD DUS GCIG TU GSAL ZHING BRTAN PAR 'CHAR THUB KYANG SKYE MCHED KYI LHA SA SNYING SOGS LA DE LTAR BYED MI NUS PA'O,,
rows.wylie: ye shes cung zad babs pa ni, gzhal yas khang dang de la bkod pa'i lha rags pa rnams nam gsal btab na yan lag nying lag thams cad dus gcig tu gsal zhing brtan par 'char thub kyang skye mched kyi lha sa snying sogs la de ltar byed mi nus pa'o
rows.english: We have then reached the level of one "upon whom a small measure of wisdom has descended" beginning with the point where--when we visualize the divine palace and all the Angels placed within it in a rough way--we are able to make out, at the same time, all the limbs and even the fingers and toes of these beings; we are able to keep the visualization firmly in our minds.  We are not though at this level capable of doing the same with the Angels of the doors of sense: the one named "Essence of Earth" and the rest.

rows.english: Here next is how we describe those who have gained some small degree of control over wisdom. The level continues on up to where the person is just about to reach the point where they have total control over wisdom.  It is stated that, at this particular juncture, there are periods not only of the stage of creation but also of the stage of completion.

rows.acip: PHYAG MTSAN NAM THIG LE PHRA MO'I NANG DU RTEN DANG BRTEN PA'I DKYIL 'KHOR YONGS RDZOGS SGOM PA NI LAS DANG PO BA DANG YE SHES CUNG ZAD BABS PA GNYIS KYI SKABS SU SGOM PA MIN GYI, YE SHES LA CUNG ZAD DBANG THOB PA NAS SGOM DGOS PAS, GNAS SKABS DANG PO GNYIS KYI DUS SU STENG 'OG GI PHYAG MTSAN NAM THIG LE PHRA MO LA SEMS 'DZIN PA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: phyag mtshan nam thig le phra mo'i nang du rten dang brten pa'i dkyil 'khor yongs rdzogs sgom pa ni las dang po ba dang ye shes cung zad babs pa gnyis kyi skabs su sgom pa min gyi, ye shes la cung zad dbang thob pa nas sgom dgos pas, gnas skabs dang po gnyis kyi dus su steng 'og gi phyag mtshan nam thig le phra mo la sems 'dzin pa yin no
rows.english: The practice of meditating upon an accoutrement of the Angel, or upon a tiny drop, and seeing within it the entire secret world--both the place and all the beings who inhabit this place--is not a meditation practice which can be done at the two levels of a beginner or one upon whom a small measure of wisdom has descended.  Rather, we must be at the level where we have gained some small degree of control over wisdom.  At the first two levels, we only hold the mind on either the accoutrement in the upper part of the scene or the lower part; or else we hold it on the tiny drop alone.

The first of these in turn will be covered in a discussion of the definition, and then a description of the various divisions of this stage.

rows.wylie: dga' bzhi skye ba thams cad byang sems 'bab pa'i rim pa sngar bshad pa ltar skye mi dgos te, rdor bzlas kyis gtum mo sbar nas byang sems zhu ba stod smad nas snying gar bsdus pa las dga' bzhi skye bar gsungs pa'i phyir, de la dpyad bya mang yang sems dben gyi skabs su cung zad 'chad do
rows.english: It's not necessarily the case that every time the four forms of bliss arise they arise in the order in which, as we explained before, the element descends.  And this is true because it is stated that--when we use the recitation of the diamonds to ignite the inner fire, and the element of enlightenment melts down and moves from the upper and lower parts of the body to gather at the heart--then the four forms of bliss occur here as well.  A great many questions are raised in this regard, which I will touch on briefly when we reach the section on transcendent mind.

rows.english: There are also certain signs which come with working at crucial points in the body.  These begin with signs such as when the winds which tend to be diverted to a great degree towards the outside, through the passageways of the organs of sense, start to turn slightly towards the inside; and then reverse their flow to some degree; and are finally injected fully into the central channel.  There are further a great number of signs which come when one has reached a high stage of the spiritual path--special signs of turning towards the inside, and reversing in flow.  These are described in the Lantern.

rows.acip: DANG PO NI, SEMS DBEN MTHAR THUG GI DPE'I 'OD GSAL LAS RLUNG CUNG ZAD G-YOS TE LUGS LDOG GI NYER THOB GRUB PA DANG DUS MNYAM DU, SEMS DBEN MTHAR THUG GI DPE'I 'OD GSAL GYIS LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN DANG DE'I BZHON PAR GYUR PA'I GNYUG RLUNG GIS NYER LEN BYAS NAS MTSAN DPES SPRAS PA'I LHA'I SKU DNGOS GNAS LA GRUB PA NAS BZUNG STE, DON GYI 'OD GSAL GYI THABS NYE BA'I RGYU RNAMS MA SKYES TSUN CHAD KYI RDZOGS RIM NI, SGYU LUS KYI RIM PA'I NGO BO'O,,
rows.wylie: dang po ni, sems dben mthar thug gi dpe'i 'od gsal las rlung cung zad g-yos te lugs ldog gi nyer thob grub pa dang dus mnyam du, sems dben mthar thug gi dpe'i 'od gsal gyis lhan cig byed rkyen dang de'i bzhon par gyur pa'i gnyug rlung gis nyer len byas nas mtshan dpes spras pa'i lha'i sku dngos gnas la grub pa nas bzung ste, don gyi 'od gsal gyi thabs nye ba'i rgyu rnams ma skyes tshun chad kyi rdzogs rim ni, sgyu lus kyi rim pa'i ngo bo'o
rows.english: Here is the essential nature then of the stage called "the illusory body": The illusory body is the stage of completion which begins with the following.  At the same point that one reaches the approximate clear light of the final end of the stage of transcendent mind--and the winds have then shifted slightly, which allows one to reach the stage of attainment during the reversal of the process--something else happens.  This is where the approximate clear light of the final end of the stage of transcendent mind provides a contributing factor, and the primordial wind upon which it rides provides a material cause, and then one attains the actual body of an Angel, embellished with all the various signs and marks of an enlightened being.  The stage of the illusory body continues from this point on up to where one is able to give rise to the immediate causes which provide the means for attaining the actual clear light.

rows.acip: GNYIS PA NI, RIM PA BZHI PA'I DON GYI 'OD GSAL DE LAS RLUNG CUNG ZAD G-YOS PA DANG DUS MNYAM DU 'OD GSAL DE'I BZHON PAR GYUR PA'I RLUNG GIS NYER LEN DANG , 'OD GSAL GYI SEMS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS DAG PA'I SGYU MA'I SKUR BZHENGS PA NAS BZUNG STE, SLOB PA MTHA'I DON GYI 'OD GSAL GYI BAR GYI RDZOGS RIM NI, SLOB BA'I ZUNG 'JUG GAM BDEN GNYIS DBYER MED KYI RDZOGS RIM GYI NGO BO 'O,,
rows.wylie: gnyis pa ni, rim pa bzhi pa'i don gyi 'od gsal de las rlung cung zad g-yos pa dang dus mnyam du 'od gsal de'i bzhon par gyur pa'i rlung gis nyer len dang , 'od gsal gyi sems kyis lhan cig byed rkyen byas pa la brten nas dag pa'i sgyu ma'i skur bzhengs pa nas bzung ste, slob pa mtha'i don gyi 'od gsal gyi bar gyi rdzogs rim ni, slob ba'i zung 'jug gam bden gnyis dbyer med kyi rdzogs rim gyi ngo bo 'o
rows.english: With this we have reached the second general step in our explanation of the one-point concentration of the two truths: the stage of completion for the two truths undivided from each other.  Here then is the essential nature of the stage called "the combination of the two, for someone who is still learning," otherwise known as "the stage of completion for the two truths undivided from each other"-- This is a stage of completion which begins from the point that one has risen up in the pure body of illusion.  This occurs when the winds have shifted slightly out of the actual clear light of the fourth stage; at this same moment, the winds which act as the vehicle for this clear light provide the material cause, and the state of mind of the clear light provides the contributing factor, for this body to come. The stage continues on up through the clear light of the very last moment that one is still a person who is learning.

Here then is the essential nature of the stage called \"the combination of the two, for someone who is still learning,\" otherwise known as \"the stage of completion for the two truths undivided from each other\"-- This is a stage of completion which begins from the point that one has risen up in the pure body of illusion.  This occurs when the winds have shifted slightly out of the actual clear light of the fourth stage; at this same moment, the winds which act as the vehicle for this clear light provide the material cause, and the state of mind of the clear light provides the contributing factor, for this body to come. rows.english: It is moreover true that there is a difference in subtlety between the clear light and the stage of attainment here--because the former is a primordial form of mind, whereas the latter is, compared to it, slightly more gross.  And the fact is that--if something is any one of the three stages of light, proliferation, and attainment--then it cannot be a primordial state of mind.  And if something which were a primordial state of mind were to become something which were not a primordial state of mind, then we could never speak of it as an inborn state of mind. Which position we're going to accept here is something that merits further examination.

Later we will make a brief presentation on (2) the six-part practice of the inner winds, in the Wheel of Time.

rows.acip: SNGAGS RIM LAS, DBU MA SBYANGS PA'I GO BA NI, SOR SDUD KYIS RTAGS BCU GCIG PO BSGRUBS PA BSAM GTAN GYIS BRTAN PAR BYAS PAS RLUNG CUNG ZAD LAS SU RUNG NAS G-YAS G-YON GYI RLUNG RANG SHUGS KYIS DBU MAR 'GRO BA RTZOM PA YIN LA, MTSAMS DE NAS G-YAS G-YON GYI RGYU BA 'GOG PA'I SBYOR BA BYAS NA GNAD DU 'GRO'O, ,DE'I GONG DU BYAS KYANG MI 'GRO BAS, YAN LAG DANG PO GNYIS NI SREG RTZOL SGOM PA'I TSAD 'DZIN NO, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: sngags rim las, dbu ma sbyangs pa'i go ba ni, sor sdud kyis rtags bcu gcig po bsgrubs pa bsam gtan gyis brtan par byas pas rlung cung zad las su rung nas g-yas g-yon gyi rlung rang shugs kyis dbu mar 'gro ba rtsom pa yin la, mtshams de nas g-yas g-yon gyi rgyu ba 'gog pa'i sbyor ba byas na gnad du 'gro'o, ,de'i gong du byas kyang mi 'gro bas, yan lag dang po gnyis ni sreg rtsol sgom pa'i tshad 'dzin no, ,zhes gsungs pa'i phyir
rows.english: The Steps on the Way of the Secret Word puts it like this-- Here's what we mean when we talk about "training the central channel."  We attain the eleven different signs by using the step of withdrawal.  We then use the step of concentration to make these stable.  Because of this, the inner winds become somewhat ready for higher work.  And with this, the winds on the right and the left begin to pass into the central channel, all on their own.  If at this point we undertake methods to stop the running of the right and left winds, it will have the desired effect.  If we attempt to do this prior to this point though, it will not.  As such, the first two steps of the six are considered the point past which we can begin our practice of mastering the inner winds.

rows.acip: DE LTAR SOR SDUD KYIS RTAGS BCU GCIG PO BSGRUBS PA DE BSAM GTAN GYI YAN LAG GIS BRTAN PAR BYAS PAS RLUNG CUNG ZAD LAS SU RUNG NAS G-YAS G-YON GYI RLUNG RANG SHUGS KYIS DBU MAR 'GRO BA RTZOM PA ZHIG BYUNG NA SOR BSAM GYI NUS PA DES RDZOGS PAS, MTSAMS DE NAS SROG RTZOL BSGOM DGOS TE,

rows.english: The component known as "concentration" then takes the eleven signs which have been brought about in this way by the step of withdrawal, and makes them more stable.  With this, the inner winds are brought to some small measure of readiness for higher work, and so the right and left winds begin to move, on their own accord, into the central channel.  The power of the steps of withdrawal and concentration is expended through this, and so at this juncture we must begin our practice of mastering the life-wind.

rows.english: Here, over a period of three years, Kyungpo Neljor was able to found 108 different monasteries, among them Shongshong.  He also gave a great many teachings of the Dharma. At some points, the monks would become complacent about their studies, and distracted form their practices.  Then Kyungpo Neljor would push them back in, by showing them different divine beings.  Some needed to see the exquisite forms of many different goddesses, while others required a whole variety of terrifying Angels: forms of the Slayer of Death.

rows.english: Bliss is triggered in your mind; stay here in meditation for a bit, in the realm of indivisible bliss and void, focused on emptiness itself.  This is what we call the "ultimate way of going for shelter." The emptiness here acts as a cause for achieving my dharma body; the bliss acts as a cause for attaining my enjoyment body; and seeing what appears to us in this state as the Angel, as myself, provides a cause for reaching my body of emanation.  And because we are meditating upon emptiness, the ultimate form of the Wish for enlightenment is also complete here.

rows.acip: 'DI'I MGRON TSAN DANG PO GSUM DNGUL CHU'I ZIN BRIS LTAR YIN ZHING, BZHI PA GDON BGEGS LAN CHAGS KYI MGRON MDUN GYI 'OG TU BSKYED DGOS PAS, DKON MCHOG SRI ZHU'I MGRON GYI 'OG TU GSANG BDAG PHYAG NA RDO RJE'I MTHA' SKOR DU, RANG GIS PHAR MGU BAR BYAS KYANG TSUR GNOD PA BYED PA'I BGEGS RIGS STONG PHRAG BRGYAD CU DANG, MGU MI MGU CUNG ZAD RE BGYIS PA LA PHAN GNOD RE SA 'JOG BYED PA'I GDON GYI RIGS SUM BRGYA DRUG CU DANG, RANG GIS SNGAR GZHAN LA GNOD PA BYAS PA'I LE LAN LUS RTEN 'DI LA 'DED MKHAN GYI NAD RIGS BZHI BRGYA RTZA BZHI'I BDAG PO SOGS MI MIN 'BYUNG PO MTHA' YAS PAS BSKOR BAR MOS,
rows.wylie: 'di'i mgron tshan dang po gsum dngul chu'i zin bris ltar yin zhing, bzhi pa gdon bgegs lan chags kyi mgron mdun gyi 'og tu bskyed dgos pas, dkon mchog sri zhu'i mgron gyi 'og tu gsang bdag phyag na rdo rje'i mtha' skor du, rang gis phar mgu bar byas kyang tshur gnod pa byed pa'i bgegs rigs stong phrag brgyad cu dang, mgu mi mgu cung zad re bgyis pa la phan gnod re sa 'jog byed pa'i gdon gyi rigs sum brgya drug cu dang, rang gis sngar gzhan la gnod pa byas pa'i le lan lus rten 'di la 'ded mkhan gyi nad rigs bzhi brgya rtsa bzhi'i bdag po sogs mi min 'byung po mtha' yas pas bskor bar mos
rows.english: The description of these first three groups follows the Notes of Ngulchu.  Next we have to visualize a fourth group, the harmful and obstructing spirits who are the "Guests of Karmic Debt," below the front of the central figure and other guests. Thus below the Jewels, the Guests of Holy Service, picture the Lord of the Secret Teachings: the Bearer of the Diamond.  He is surrounded by a limitless number of inhuman creatures and evil beings, including the heads of the various different types of spirits. Here first are the 80,000 kinds of "obstructing spirits," the ones who want to harm us even if we try to appease them.  Then there are the 360 kinds of "malevolent spirits," those who we can somewhat expect to help or harm us, if we do some small thing to please or displease them.  Finally there are the 404 kinds of "sickness spirits": those whom I have harmed in my past lives and who now pursue my body, hoping to pay me back.

rows.acip: RANG LAS CHES LHAG PA MTHONG BA NA 'DI NGA LAS CUNG ZAD LHAG PA TZAM YIN GYI GZHAN 'DRA'O SNYAM PA'I CUNG ZAD MNYAM PA'I NGA RGYAL, RNYED BKUR GYIS KUN NAS BLANGS TE GRONG CHOG SOGS BYED PA NA GZHAN DON YIN SNYAM PA LTA BU LOG PA'I NGA RGYAL DANG, ZAG BCAS NYER LEN GYI PHUNG PO LA DMIGS NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU 'DZIN PA NGA'O SNYAM PA'I NGA RGYAL TE NGA RGYAL MI 'DRA BA BDUN TZAM YOD PA LAS,
rows.wylie: rang las ches lhag pa mthong ba na 'di nga las cung zad lhag pa tsam yin gyi gzhan 'dra'o snyam pa'i cung zad mnyam pa'i nga rgyal, rnyed bkur gyis kun nas blangs te grong chog sogs byed pa na gzhan don yin snyam pa lta bu log pa'i nga rgyal dang, zag bcas nyer len gyi phung po la dmigs nas nga'o snyam du 'dzin pa nga'o snyam pa'i nga rgyal te nga rgyal mi 'dra ba bdun tsam yod pa las
rows.english: "Little-bit-better but equal pride" is when you see someone who is much higher than you are, and you think that they are just a little higher than you in that one thing, and that you are equal to them in everything else. "Mistaken pride" is when you do a house-ritual or some other service motivated by a desire for money and fame, but think to yourself that you are doing it in order to help other people. What we call the "pride that thinks 'me'" focuses on the impure parts of your body and mind which you have taken on at birth, and thinks that they are "me," meaning that we grasp to them as "me."  Thus there are some seven different kinds of pride.

rows.english: In the Angel's left hand She holds a skullcup: Her holy mind, forever filled with great bliss.  She lifts the cup up high, and tilts it slightly. rows.english: On her left shoulder is a khatvanga staff.  The bottom of the staff leans forward, and the tip leans back.  Generally speaking, the staff can represent many different things.  It means that She is never separated from Her white element, and it also symbolizes emptiness and the Man of the partnership.  The main meaning here is of Her partner, which I will explain in more detail.

rows.acip: DE RNAMS MA BRJED PA'I MU NAS SHANGS MTHO ZHING SHANGS BUG SHIN TU GTZANG ZHING DMAR SENG NGE BA, DE NAS ZHAL CUNG ZAD GDANGS PA HE BYAS PA LTA BU, TSEMS DKAR ZHING THAGS BZANG BA BZHI BCU TSANG BA, MCHE BA NAS 'BRU TZAM YAS MAS SU GNYIS RE YOD PA, TSEMS KYI BAR NAS SHIN TU SRAB CING DMAR BA'I LJAGS CUNG ZAD MTHONG BA,
rows.wylie: de rnams ma brjed pa'i mu nas shangs mtho zhing shangs bug shin tu gtsang zhing dmar seng nge ba, de nas zhal cung zad gdangs pa he byas pa lta bu, tshems dkar zhing thags bzang ba bzhi bcu tshang ba, mche ba nas 'bru tsam yas mas su gnyis re yod pa, tshems kyi bar nas shin tu srab cing dmar ba'i ljags cung zad mthong ba
rows.english: Staying in a state where you maintain what you are visualizing so far, focus then on Her nose.  It is high, and its two nostril are totally clean and a healthy red inside.  Her mouth is cracked open in a subtle smile. Her teeth are pearly white; She has all forty complete, and they are lined up nicely in perfect order. rows.english: The Diamond Angel possesses six different aspects. The fact that She is standing in the middle of a wisdom fire and twisting slightly to the left represents that She is alluring.  The fact that She is stamping on top of the Frightener and the Lady of the Night represents Her fearlessness. These are the two aspect of Her body. Her subtle half-smile represents that She can be wild, and baring Her fangs represents that She can be frightening. These are the two aspects of Her speech. Her doe eyes represent Her compassion, and the intensity of Her gaze represents Her ferocity. These are the two aspects of Her thoughts.

rows.english: With your body then you are doing the following.  You are using your hands to make the sign.  Release your legs out of the full lotus position, to where your two knees are still bent, slightly raised.  The positioning of the legs now is such that you are pressing down your right big toe with your left.  Lower your eyes slightly, and then in one motion raise them from the left up to the sky, at the same time raising the sign from your left knee into the air before the middle of your forehead.  With the sign make three circles counter-clockwise, and then three clockwise, and finally three more counter-clockwise.

rows.english: The various treatises of the Sakya tradition state that here, at the point when you perform the first practice of the completion stage, you should pull in a bit of lower wind, as a sort of harbinger of things to come.  Then press the upper wind down on top of it.  Then breathe in the lower wind all the way.  Finish this process of pulling in and pressing down three times, the texts state, and thus make what is called the "capsule."  These three winds, they say, represent the mouth, the base, and the body of a pitcher.

rows.english: There are four crucial points for starting this practice.  If you are mainly working on emptiness, then you should practice at daybreak, and if you are focusing mainly on bliss, you should practice at sunset.  This is the crucial point of the time of day.  Your meditation seat should be a little higher in the back, and lower in the front.  The crucial point of the body is to assume the seven or eight-point posture of Appearances.  The crucial point of the winds is to do the nine-part breathing practice, and the crucial point of the body is to do the visualization of the three channels and the four chakras. rows.acip: DE NAS NU MA GNYIS LA LTOS PA'I DKYIL, RGYAB MDUN GNYIS LA LTOS PA'I RGYAB LA CUNG ZAD NYE BAR RTA DBU MA RGYUN PAR PHYI SNGON PO DANG, GTUM MO'I TSE DMAR PO KHO NA SBOM PHRA MDA' SNYUG TZAM MAR SNA LTE BA NAS YAR SNE THOD PA'I 'OG KLAD RGYA'I STENG NAS SBA GUG PA LTAR KHYOGS TE YE SHES KYI SPYAN GYI THAD DU ZUG PA,
rows.wylie: de nas nu ma gnyis la ltos pa'i dkyil, rgyab mdun gnyis la ltos pa'i rgyab la cung zad nye bar rta dbu ma rgyun par phyi sngon po dang, gtum mo'i tshe dmar po kho na sbom phra mda' snyug tsam mar sna lte ba nas yar sne thod pa'i 'og klad rgya'i steng nas sba gug pa ltar khyogs te ye shes kyi spyan gyi thad du zug pa
rows.english: Next visualize your central channel.  It is located at the plane in between your two nipples.  If you were to draw a line down the very middle of your body, it is a little bit closer to the back.  Usually it is blue, but when you are doing the practice of inner fire you should visualize it as red.  Its width is the same as that of the shaft of a narrow arrow [or an American drinking straw.]  The lower opening is at your navel, and the upper opening goes under your skull, over your brain, and then bends over the top of your head terminating at the place in between your two eyebrows.

rows.english: If you are going to hold your breath in this practice, first bring up the lower wind slightly.  Picture that at the same time the lower bliss swirl at the lower opening begins to swirl up your central channel filling your body and mind with ecstasy. It travels up Her central channel and then goes through the bottom of the dharma star at Her heart, through the moon disk, and enters into the lower half of the vam syllable.  Picture that it is spinning inside the cavity of the vam syllable.

rows.acip: MI THUB PA 'DRA NA BTZAN THABS SU MI BZUNG BAR 'OG RLUNG 'THAN NE BA'I NGANG NAS SNA SGO'I SPU MI 'GUL BA'I TSOD KYIS DAL BUS BTANG LA, CUNG ZAD NGAL GSOS LA YANG 'DZIN PA SOGS GANG THUB KYI SGO NAS YID BZLAS BYA,

rows.english: When it seems as though you won't be able to retain the breath any longer, don't struggle to hold it.  Milk the lower wind gently upwards and release your breath so gently that it doesn't even cause the hairs in your nostrils to sway.  Then take a bit of a break to rest yourself, and then repeat the retention, for as long as you are comfortably able--repeating the mantra as you go.

rows.english: The practice of transfer has been called the "instruction for persons of many bad deeds to reach enlightenment by force." rows.acip: SINDH'U RA'I ZHABS KYI DGA' 'KHYIL GYI PAR RANG GI DPRAL BAR BTAB LA ME LONG KHYER TE PAR HA CANG GSAL NA CUNG ZAD MI MNGON PAR BYAS,

rows.english: You'll recall that we had carved a little bliss swirl into the small wooden plug at the bottom of the container; use it now to take some of the powder and press an image of a bliss swirl into the middle of your forehead. If it is, then wipe it a bit until it's sort of hard to see.

rows.english: This brings us to the third step in the practice of sindhura: the sacred work.  Here first you dress up as a kusali--a wandering hermit: it would appear that just your normal old street clothes would be fine.  Make an imprint on your forehead of a bliss swirl, using the sindhura powder.  Carry a little hand-mirror with you so that you can check how the swirl looks: if it's too obvious, then smear it away a bit.  Keep the trunk container with you, but in such a way that others can't see it.

rows.acip: BDUD RTZI'I DVANGS MA RNAMS SNYING GAR SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD KYI NGO BO RJE BTZUN MA'I THUGS DANG RANG SEMS DBYER MED BAm YIG GI RNAM PAR GNAS PA LA THIMS PAS BDE STONG GI RTOGS PA SKYES PAR BSAM LA CUNG ZAD MNYAM PAR 'JOG PA STE,
rows.wylie: bdud rtsi'i dvangs ma rnams snying gar sangs rgyas thams cad kyi ngo bo rje btsun ma'i thugs dang rang sems dbyer med baM yig gi rnam par gnas pa la thims pas bde stong gi rtogs pa skyes par bsam la cung zad mnyam par 'jog pa ste
rows.english: The pure essences of the nectar then dissolve into your heart, and due to this, the pure mind of the Holy Angel, whose true nature is that of every Buddha, becomes indivisible with your mind (which appears in the form of a vam syllable at your heart). rows.english: However, it doesn't seem to me that all three of these instructions were meant to be put into practice at that time.  If that were the case, then instead of putting into practice that which is carried out during the stage of completion--the practice called the shared inconceivable--we would be doing the practice known as the unique inconceivable, which is connected with the stage of creation, and used mainly for reaching outer heaven, like those practices such as Langali.  And to a mind as dull as mine, this wouldn't make much sense. _______________

rows.acip: BLUN RMONGS YON TAN GYI RDUL DRIS MA GOS PA BDAG CAG NI SNYING NAS PHYAG 'TSAL ZHING SKYABS SU MCHIS LAS MA 'DAS KYANG, 'DI SKOR LA SNGA MO TI TUG KHA SHAS NAS PHRAG DOG KHO NA'I BYED PAS CAL COL SMRA BA BYUNG ZHING, ZIN BRIS SU YANG MDOR BSDUS LAS MED PAS RANG LUGS 'DZIN PA RNAMS KYI DOGS PA SEL PHYIR CUNG ZAD SPROS TE BRIS PA YIN NO,

rows.english: Us ignorant fools, who are not graced with so much as an atom of their high qualities, can't do more than bow down to them from our hearts and go for refuge.  But it has happened that a few mulish souls have babbled on about this issue previously, simply out of jealousy.  And so, because there is no more than a passing mention in the Notes, and in order to dispel any confusion for those who embrace our own system, I have written this small elaboration on the subject. rows.english: What this is saying is that those of wisdom grasp the following.  The very essence of all things--whether they relate to the person or to the things that make up a person--is that they occur through dependence on their particular causes and conditions: they are projections based on something else.  As such they do not exist as something which is real or "pure."  They possess not even the slightest bit of any nature which could ever exist in and of itself.

rows.acip: GNYID DU 'GRO BA'I DUS SU SNYING KHA DANG NOR BUR RLUNG 'DU TSABS CHE LA, DE 'THUG PA'I RING LA RMI LAM MED PA'I GNYID 'ONG NGO, ,DE NAS GNAS DE GNYIS NAS RLUNG CUNG ZAD SRAB TU SONG NAS, MGRIN PA DANG GSANG GNAS SU 'ONGS PA NA RMI LAM 'CHAR LA, DER 'DUS PA'I RING LA RMI LAM NYID 'BYUNG NGO, ,DE NAS RLUNG GNAS DE NYID NAS GYES TE DPRAL BA DANG LTE BAR SONG NAS SAD PAR 'GYUR RO,,
rows.wylie: gnyid du 'gro ba'i dus su snying kha dang nor bur rlung 'du tshabs che la, de 'thug pa'i ring la rmi lam med pa'i gnyid 'ong ngo, ,de nas gnas de gnyis nas rlung cung zad srab tu song nas, mgrin pa dang gsang gnas su 'ongs pa na rmi lam 'char la, der 'dus pa'i ring la rmi lam nyid 'byung ngo, ,de nas rlung gnas de nyid nas gyes te dpral ba dang lte bar song nas sad par 'gyur ro
rows.english: When you are falling off to sleep, there is a very strong concentration of wind at the heart and at the jewel.  When this concentration increases, you go into dreamless sleep.  When the wind in these two places begins to fade slightly, then it moves to the throat and the secret place, and dreams start to come to you.  You stay in this same state of dreams as long as the winds remain concentrated in these two spots. Finally the winds branch off from these two points and pass to the forehead and the navel--upon which you awake.

rows.acip: DE NAS NU MA GNYIS LA LTOS PA'I DKYIL, RGYAB MDUN GNYIS LA LTOS PA'I RGYAB LA CUNG ZAD NYE BAR RTZA DBU MA RGYUN PAR PHYI SNGON PO DANG, GTUM MO'I TSE DMAR PO KHO NA SBOM PHRA MDA' SNYUG TZAM MAR SNA LTE BA NAS YAR SNE THOD PA'I 'OG KLAD RGYA'I STENG NAS SBA GUG PA LTAR KHYOGS TE YE SHES KYI SPYAN GYI THAD DU ZUG PA,
rows.wylie: de nas nu ma gnyis la ltos pa'i dkyil, rgyab mdun gnyis la ltos pa'i rgyab la cung zad nye bar rtsa dbu ma rgyun par phyi sngon po dang, gtum mo'i tshe dmar po kho na sbom phra mda' snyug tsam mar sna lte ba nas yar sne thod pa'i 'og klad rgya'i steng nas sba gug pa ltar khyogs te ye shes kyi spyan gyi thad du zug pa
rows.english: Next visualize your central channel.  It is located at the midline of the body, in between your two nipples.  Relative to the plane of the front and back of the body, it is a little bit closer to the back.  Usually it is blue on the outside, but when you are doing the practice of inner fire you should visualize it as pure red.  Its width is the same as that of the shaft of a narrow arrow [or an American drinking straw.]  The lower opening is at your navel, and up above it goes under your skull, over your brain, and then bends like a cane over the top of your head, with the upper opening reaching to the place in between your two eyebrows.

rows.acip: RDZOGS RIM DANG PO 'DI'I SKABS SA LUGS LA KHRID YIG TU GSUNGS PA LTAR DANG POR 'OG RLUNG SNYAN GSAN 'BEB PA'I TSUL DU CUNG ZAD 'THEN, DE NAS STENG RLUNG MNAN, DE NAS 'OG RLUNG RDZOGS PAR RNGUB STE STENG 'OG GI RLUNG 'THEN THEBS GSUM BYAS TE KHA SBYOR BYA BAR GSUNGS SHING, RLUNG GSUM PO DES BUM PA'I KHA ZHABS LTO BA GSUM MTSON PAR GSUNGS KYANG,
rows.wylie: rdzogs rim dang po 'di'i skabs sa lugs la khrid yig tu gsungs pa ltar dang por 'og rlung snyan gsan 'beb pa'i tshul du cung zad 'then, de nas steng rlung mnan, de nas 'og rlung rdzogs par rngub ste steng 'og gi rlung 'then thebs gsum byas te kha sbyor bya bar gsungs shing, rlung gsum po des bum pa'i kha zhabs lto ba gsum mtshon par gsungs kyang
rows.english: The various treatises of the Sakya tradition state that here, at the point when you perform the first practice of the completion stage, you should pull in a bit of lower wind, as a sort of harbinger of things to come.  Then press the upper wind down on top of it.  Then breathe in the lower wind all the way.  Finish this process of pulling in and pressing down three times, the texts state, and thus make what is called the "capsule."  These three winds, they say, represent the mouth, the base, and the body of a pitcher.

rows.english: The next step begins by seeing yourself as the close Angel. rows.english: If you are going to hold your breath in this practice, first bring up the lower wind slightly.  Picture that at the same time the bliss swirl at the lower opening begins to swirl up your central channel, filling your body and mind with ecstasy.  As it rises up it penetrates the dharma star and moon at your heart effortlessly, and then enters into the central Angel through Her clitoris.  It travels up Her central channel and then goes through the bottom point of the dharma star at Her heart, through the moon disk, and enters into the lower half of the vam syllable.  Picture that it is spinning inside the cavity of the vam syllable.

rows.acip: DE LTAR BYAS KYANG RLUNG DBU MAR 'DU BA LA DE TZAM MI PHAN PA'I PHYIR TE, YUD CIG GI RING LA, SPRUL PA'I 'KHOR LO'I DBUS SU BZUNG BA DE YUN CUNG ZAD RE LAS DER MI GNAS PAR PHYIR LA 'PHYUGS 'GRO BA'I PHYIR DANG, 'KHOR LO'I DBUS LAS PHYIR RING BAR RLUNG ZIN PA LA, DROD DANG BDE BA THAN THUN SKYE YANG SROG DH'U T'IR TSUD PA LA PHAN CHUNG BA'I PHYIR RO,,
rows.wylie: de ltar byas kyang rlung dbu mar 'du ba la de tsam mi phan pa'i phyir te, yud cig gi ring la, sprul pa'i 'khor lo'i dbus su bzung ba de yun cung zad re las der mi gnas par phyir la 'phyugs 'gro ba'i phyir dang, 'khor lo'i dbus las phyir ring bar rlung zin pa la, drod dang bde ba than thun skye yang srog dhU tIr tshud pa la phan chung ba'i phyir ro
rows.english: The point here is that, if you do hold the wind after it has become uncomfortable, it doesn't help you in any significant way to gather the winds into the central channel.  Hold the wind for a touch; if you keep it there in the center of the chakra of emanation for anything more than that, it won't stay there anyway: it slips out.  It is true that, if you sit there holding the wind outside the center of this chakra for an extended period of time, you will get some minor feelings of warmth and pleasure; but this is of very little help in the task of getting the life wind injected into the channel of dance.

rows.acip: THABS SNGA MA LA 'BYUNG BA LA YANG PHYIN CI LOG GI SA'I RLUNG LA SOGS PA RNAMS LDOG RUNG DU SONG BA DANG, CUNG ZAD LOG PA DANG GTAN NAS LOG PA'I RTAGS GSUM 'ONG BAR BSHAD PA LTAR, DBANG PO'I SGO RNAMS NAS PHYIR HA CANG GA YO BA'I RLUNG CUNG ZAD NANG DU LDOG PAR RTZOM PA DANG, CUNG ZAD LOG PA DANG, DBU MAR CUNG ZAD TSUD PA SOGS KYI RTAGS NAS BZUNG STE,
rows.wylie: thabs snga ma la 'byung ba la yang phyin ci log gi sa'i rlung la sogs pa rnams ldog rung du song ba dang, cung zad log pa dang gtan nas log pa'i rtags gsum 'ong bar bshad pa ltar, dbang po'i sgo rnams nas phyir ha cang ga yo ba'i rlung cung zad nang du ldog par rtsom pa dang, cung zad log pa dang, dbu mar cung zad tshud pa sogs kyi rtags nas bzung ste
rows.english: When the signs occur in relation to the former method, three are explained as happening in conjunction with three stages that occur with undesirable winds relating to the element of earth and the rest; that is, where these winds are getting close to stopping; where they have in part stopped; and where they stop completely. These correspond to states of the winds related to the doors of sense--winds which are excessively active.  These states would be where these winds have just started to turn inwards; where they have turned in slightly; where they have been slightly inserted into the central channel; and so on.

rows.wylie: dang po ni, lugs 'di la gtum mo sgom nas rlung dbu mar 'dzud pa dgos zhes pa gsal bar snang yang, srog dhU tIr tshud pa la brten nas sgyu lus dang, 'od gsal gnyis sgom tshul shin tu mi gsal zhing, de rnams shin tu rtogs dka' bar byung snang mod kyang, 'dir man ngag la go ba thun mong ma yin pa chags pa'i phyir du cung zad cig brjod par bya'o
rows.english: Here is the first.  Now the teachings on this practice clearly state that one must get the winds to enter the central channel by utilizing the practice of inner fire.  They are extremely unclear though on how you're supposed to practice reaching the pair of the body of illusion and the clear light by utilizing your successful attempt to get the life winds to move into this channel of dance.  It is moreover quite apparent that we are talking about stages that are very difficult to actually have a personal experience of.  Nonetheless I am going to say a bit about these points here, so that you can eventually come to a very special understanding of the advices of this tradition.

rows.acip: MDOR NA NGA'O SNYAM DU 'DZIN PA'I GZHI GANG ZAG LA, PHUNG PO DANG RANG BZHIN CIG THA DAD GANG DU GRUB SNYAM DU BRTAGS PA'I SGO NAS, GANG ZAG LA RANG BZHIN CUNG ZAD KYANG MED DO SNYAM PA'I NGES PA BRTAN PO BYA STE, STONG PHYOGS LA DE 'DRA BA MANG DU SBYANG,
rows.wylie: mdor na nga'o snyam du 'dzin pa'i gzhi gang zag la, phung po dang rang bzhin cig tha dad gang du grub snyam du brtags pa'i sgo nas, gang zag la rang bzhin cung zad kyang med do snyam pa'i nges pa brtan po bya ste, stong phyogs la de 'dra ba mang du sbyang
rows.english: In short, you must take this thing you are focusing on when you think "me"--you must take this person--and do an analysis, thinking to yourself whether it could be one and the same as its parts, the heaps, or whether it could be divorced from them. In this way you will come to a very firm understanding wherein you think to yourself, "This 'person' doesn't have even the very slightest nature of its own." Practice thinking this way, about the emptiness side of things, over and over.

rows.english: Now if you make a special effort like this to come to a good understanding of all the crucial points of the various instructions for the practice of dreams, you will come to be a true master of it--one with authentic experience. rows.english: If the image of the drop gets too bright, you will either find yourself unable to sleep or--even if you do sleep some--you wake very quickly. If this happens, make the image a little less vivid.

rows.acip: RMI LAM LA RMI LAM DU SHES PA DE DPE LA BLANGS NAS, CHOS GZHAN THAMS CAD KYANG DE DANG 'DRA BAR BDEN PAR GRUB PA CUNG ZAD KYANG MED DO SNYAM DU NGES PAR BYA STE, BDEN 'DZIN GYIS JI LTAR BZUNG BA LEGS PAR SHES NAS DES BZUNG BA LTAR MED PA'I RGYU MTSAN YANG DAG RNAMS SHES DGOS SO,,
rows.wylie: rmi lam la rmi lam du shes pa de dpe la blangs nas, chos gzhan thams cad kyang de dang 'dra bar bden par grub pa cung zad kyang med do snyam du nges par bya ste, bden 'dzin gyis ji ltar bzung ba legs par shes nas des bzung ba ltar med pa'i rgyu mtshan yang dag rnams shes dgos so
rows.english: You must come to a point where you can take the example of recognizing a dream as a dream and reach a current understanding of things, where you say to yourself, "Every single other thing that exists is the same way: just like the things in dreams, they are devoid of a single shred of true existence."  In short, you have to become very familiar with how our tendency to hold things as real grasps on to what it thinks it sees, and then you have to study well all the true reasons why things cannot be as it thinks they are.

rows.acip: DE YANG SAD DUS KYI YID NGO'I SNANG BA DANG, RMI LAM GYI YID NGO'I SNANG BA GNYIS PHYI MA SDUD PA CHES SLA LA, DE'I DUS SU RLUNG SHIN TU RAGS PA 'GA' ZHIG THIM YOD PA'I GNOD KYIS, SLAR YANG RLUNG SNYING KHAR 'DU ZHING RMI LAM GYI SNANG BA MI 'CHAR BAR GNYID DU 'GRO'O, ,DE'I TSE GNYID KYI STONG PA RNAMS CUNG ZAD NGES NUS LA,
rows.wylie: de yang sad dus kyi yid ngo'i snang ba dang, rmi lam gyi yid ngo'i snang ba gnyis phyi ma sdud pa ches sla la, de'i dus su rlung shin tu rags pa 'ga' zhig thim yod pa'i gnod kyis, slar yang rlung snying khar 'du zhing rmi lam gyi snang ba mi 'char bar gnyid du 'gro'o, ,de'i tshe gnyid kyi stong pa rnams cung zad nges nus la
rows.english: Now of the two--of the things that appear before your awareness in your waking hours, and the things that appear to your awareness during your dreams--the latter are infinitely more easy to withdraw this way.  When you do this visualization, certain very gross forms of wind actually dissolve; due to this crucial point you can then gather the winds at your heart, go off to sleep without having any dreams, and find yourself able--slightly--to perceive at this juncture the different forms of the emptiness of sleep.

rows.acip: SNA BUG GNYIS NAS STENG RLUNG RNGUB CHUNG GSUM BRNGUBS PAS RTZA GSUM GYI SNE NAS ZHUGS TE LTAG PA'I RLUNG LA PHOG PAS DE G-YOS NAS, HAm GI KLAD KOR GYI 'OD KYI GTUM MO KshUm LAS ME SNGAR BZHIN 'BAR BA DBU MA'I NANG NAS MAR SONG BA'I ME RLUNG GIS, MAS NAS YONG BA'I ME RLUNG THAMS CAD THUR DU MNAN TE, SNYING GA'I THAD KYI DBU MA'I NANG DU STENG 'OG GI ME GNYIS 'KHRUG CING 'THAB PA'I ME 'OD LA SEMS GTAD NAS RLUNG KHA SBYAR BUM CAN LUS CUNG ZAD 'GUL ZHING CI THUB BZUNG BA LAN 'GA' BYAS PA'I MTHAR,
rows.wylie: sna bug gnyis nas steng rlung rngub chung gsum brngubs pas rtsa gsum gyi sne nas zhugs te ltag pa'i rlung la phog pas de g-yos nas, haM gi klad kor gyi 'od kyi gtum mo kShuM las me sngar bzhin 'bar ba dbu ma'i nang nas mar song ba'i me rlung gis, mas nas yong ba'i me rlung thams cad thur du mnan te, snying ga'i thad kyi dbu ma'i nang du steng 'og gi me gnyis 'khrug cing 'thab pa'i me 'od la sems gtad nas rlung kha sbyar bum can lus cung zad 'gul zhing ci thub bzung ba lan 'ga' byas pa'i mthar
rows.english: Inhale three short breaths of upper wind from both nostrils.  With this, the wind enters in from the ends of the three channels and strikes the wind at the back of the head, arousing it.  Then that same type of sharp flame as before now shoots out from the kshum, which is the inner fire of light--the one inside the circle of the ham.  The flame burns down the inside of the central channel as wind and fire, pressing down into all the fire and wind coming up from below.  These two upper and lower flames meet inside the central channel at the area of the heart; they clash and become entangled. Place the mind into this skirmish of fire and light, and hold the winds in a vase, shaking the body a little.  Do this several times, holding for as long as you can.

rows.acip: KUN RTOG GI RLUNG SEMS LA THIM PA'I PHYI RTAGS NI, DBUGS PHYIR RING DU RGYU ZHING NANG DU SDUD MI SHES, CUNG ZAD SDUD KYANG THUNG LA RTZUB PAR SDUD, NANG RTAGS MAR ME RLUNG GIS MA BSKYOD PA LTA BU 'BYUNG,
rows.wylie: kun rtog gi rlung sems la thim pa'i phyi rtags ni, dbugs phyir ring du rgyu zhing nang du sdud mi shes, cung zad sdud kyang thung la rtsub par sdud, nang rtags mar me rlung gis ma bskyod pa lta bu 'byung
rows.english: As the wind of conceptualization dissolves into the mind, the outer sign is that the exhalation of breath is lengthened, and you lose your ability to breathe it back again.  Even if you can inhale a bit, the breath is very short and raspy.  The inner sign is an impression of something similar to a candle flame which is totally still, in a place without the slightest draft of air to move it.

rows.english: Before Her, And behind Her, Race Crocodile-Face And Lion-Face, Bent on wasting the lives Of any foe She has. rows.acip: YANG SNGAR BZHIN 'DZIN PA'I ME GSO BA LAN BDUN TZAM BYAS PAS, Rm YIG JE DMAR LA SONG NAS ME STAG DMAR KHROM KHROM DANG , DE YANG JE CHER SONG NAS ME 'OD CUNG ZAD 'PHRO BAS RTZA SBUGS THAMS CAD DMAR SENG SENG SONG BAR BSAM,
rows.wylie: yang sngar bzhin 'dzin pa'i me gso ba lan bdun tsam byas pas, rM yig je dmar la song nas me stag dmar khrom khrom dang , de yang je cher song nas me 'od cung zad 'phro bas rtsa sbugs thams cad dmar seng seng song bar bsam
rows.english: Then stoke the fire about seven times, holding as above.  The letter ram [ram%] becomes even more red, and it starts shooting out a shower of red sparks. rows.acip: DANG PO BSAM GTAN GYI STAN LA ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR, STAN NI GAL CHE BA YIN PAS 'BOL ZHING YA YO MED PAR RGYAB CUNG ZAD MTHO BAR BYAS LA,
rows.wylie: dang po bsam gtan gyi stan la zhes gsungs pa ltar, stan ni gal che ba yin pas 'bol zhing ya yo med par rgyab cung zad mtho bar byas la
rows.english: As for the first, we begin with--as the text says--"coming to the seat for meditation."  The seat that you use for your practice is of great importance; it should have a cushion without lumps in it, and should be stable so that it doesn't shift around.  The back of the cushion should be a bit higher than the front.

rows.acip: KUN RTOG GI RLUNG SEMS LA THIM PA'I PHYI RTAGS NI, DBUGS PHYIR RING DU RGYU ZHING NANG DU SDUD MI SHES, CUNG ZAD SDUD KYANG THUNG LA RTZUB PAR SDUD, NANG RTAGS MAR ME RLUNG GIS MA BSKYOD PA LTA BU 'BYUNG,
rows.wylie: kun rtog gi rlung sems la thim pa'i phyi rtags ni, dbugs phyir ring du rgyu zhing nang du sdud mi shes, cung zad sdud kyang thung la rtsub par sdud, nang rtags mar me rlung gis ma bskyod pa lta bu 'byung
rows.english: As the wind of conceptualization dissolves into the mind, the outer sign is that the exhalation of breath is lengthened, and you lose your ability to breathe it back again.  Even if you can inhale a bit, the breath is very short and raspy.  The inner sign is an impression of something similar to a candle flame which is totally still, in a place without the slightest draft of air to move it.

rows.acip: DES NA KHAMS BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS ZHU BA LAS BYUNG BA MIN PAR, DRAN SHES KYI SEMS BYING RGOD DANG BRAL BA'I MI RTOG PA TZAM BSKYANGS PAS, RLUNG CUNG ZAD LAS SU RUNG BA LAS SKYES PA'I BDE GSAL MI RTOG PA ZHES ZER BA'I BDE BA YANG MIN LA,
rows.wylie: des na khams byang chub kyi sems zhu ba las byung ba min par, dran shes kyi sems bying rgod dang bral ba'i mi rtog pa tsam bskyangs pas, rlung cung zad las su rung ba las skyes pa'i bde gsal mi rtog pa zhes zer ba'i bde ba yang min la
rows.english: As such, the practice of maintaining no more than some non-conceptual state of mind, a mind full of awareness and watchfulness, free of all mental dullness or agitation--since it is not something which has come about through the meltdown of the essential substance, the element of enlightenment--does not even qualify as that kind of bliss they call the "non-conceptual state of bliss and clarity," which you get when the winds are just slightly well-practiced.

rows.acip: SNGAR BSHAD PA BZHIN SGYU LUS DANG 'OD GSAL GNYIS KA 'PHAGS SKOR GYI GDAMS NGAG DANG SGRIGS RGYUR SNANG LA, BSHAD MA THAG PA'I 'OD GSAL DU 'JUG TSUL NI, GSANG 'DUS RIM LNGA'I RJES GZHIG GI BSAM GTAN KHYAD PAR CAN DU SNANG BAS, 'DUS PA'I GDAMS NGAG GIS CUNG ZAD BRGYAN NAS BSHAD DO,,
rows.wylie: sngar bshad pa bzhin sgyu lus dang 'od gsal gnyis ka 'phags skor gyi gdams ngag dang sgrigs rgyur snang la, bshad ma thag pa'i 'od gsal du 'jug tshul ni, gsang 'dus rim lnga'i rjes gzhig gi bsam gtan khyad par can du snang bas, 'dus pa'i gdams ngag gis cung zad brgyan nas bshad do
rows.english: As I explained earlier, it seems best to treat the two subjects of the body of illusion and the clear light in accordance with the books of advice upon the system of the realized being Nagarjuna.  As for the presentation I have just made on how to enter into the clear light, it appears to me that the meditative practice found in the Five Stages of the Secret Collection for erasing things as you withdraw the visualization is an extraordinary method; and so I have enriched my explanation here with just a bit from the books of advice on the Collection.

rows.acip: 'DI'I GDAMS NGAG SHOG DRIL BZHI PA'I 'PHO BA DANG, RNGOG LUGS KYI GDAMS NGAG RNAMS KYI 'PHO BA'I DMIGS PA DNGOS GZHI RNAMS CUNG RGYAS PAR SNANG YANG, 'DIR LUGS 'DI'I MAN NGAG GTZO BOR MDZAD PA'I BLA MA RNAMS KYI MAN NGAG NAS 'BYUNG BA CUNG ZAD BRJOD PAR BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: 'di'i gdams ngag shog dril bzhi pa'i 'pho ba dang, rngog lugs kyi gdams ngag rnams kyi 'pho ba'i dmigs pa dngos gzhi rnams cung rgyas par snang yang, 'dir lugs 'di'i man ngag gtso bor mdzad pa'i bla ma rnams kyi man ngag nas 'byung ba cung zad brjod par bya'o
rows.english: It would seem that the main part of the practice for the visualizations we need as we send our consciousness on is described in somewhat greater detail in both Four Pages on the Practice of Sending on the Mind, a book of advices on these points, and in the various books of advice in the Ngok tradition.  Here though I will turn for a bit to the personal advices of the Lamas who have made the instructions of this particular practice their primary practice.

rows.acip: DE NAS THIG LE MCHOG MA'I SGRUB THABS BSHAD PA, TZANDAN DANG, 'O MA'I ZAS LA KHRI BZLAS NAS NYI MA BDUN NA MCHOD PA RGYAS PAR BYAS TE YAR GYI NGO'I TSES BRGYAD LA RI'I RTZE MOR SONG LA MTSAN THOG THAG BZLAS NA THO RANGS NGES PAR 'ONGS TE CUNG ZAD RGOD PAS CHAGS PA BYAS NAS MDUN DU SDOD DO,,
rows.wylie: de nas thig le mchog ma'i sgrub thabs bshad pa, tsandan dang, 'o ma'i zas la khri bzlas nas nyi ma bdun na mchod pa rgyas par byas te yar gyi ngo'i tshes brgyad la ri'i rtse mor song la mtshan thog thag bzlas na tho rangs nges par 'ongs te cung zad rgod pas chags pa byas nas mdun du sdod do
rows.english: Next we explain a ritual for reaching the Lady of the Ultimate Drop, Tilottama.  Set out a small torma cake which has mixed in it both sandalwood and milk.  For the length of seven days, make extensive offerings, and then on the eighth day of the waxing moon climb a high mountain peak.  Spend the whole night there reciting mantas, and at daybreak She will without doubt come to you.  She acts a little wild, and will stand in front of you in a pose of passion.

rows.acip: 'DI BYUNG BA'I DUS NI RNAM THAR GZHAN RNAMS SU SNYUN CUNG ZAD DVANGS PA'I DUS ZHES PA LAS GSAL CHA MI 'DUG KYANG, PAn CHEN BLO GROS LEGS BZANG GIS MDZAD PA'I GSANG RNAM DU, SHING RTA LO ZLA BA DANG PO'I NANG YIN PAR GSUNGS 'DUG ,
rows.wylie: 'di byung ba'i dus ni rnam thar gzhan rnams su snyun cung zad dvangs pa'i dus zhes pa las gsal cha mi 'dug kyang, paN chen blo gros legs bzang gis mdzad pa'i gsang rnam du, shing rta lo zla ba dang po'i nang yin par gsungs 'dug
rows.english: Concerning the exact dating of these events, the other biographies only say that they happened "at a time when Je Tsongkapa had somewhat recovered from an illness," and nothing more precise than this.  The secret biography composed by Panchen Lodru Leksang though states that these incidents took place in the first month of the Wood Horse Year [1414]. ....

rows.acip: SKABS 'DIR RJE RTOGS LDAN PAR MNAL LTAS BYUNG TSUL SKOR, MKHAS GRUB THAMS CAD MKHYEN PAS MDZAD PA'I GSANG RNAM SOGS SU GONG DU BKOD PA LTAR BYUNG ZHING, RJE BLO GROS LEGS BZANG GIS MDZAD PA'I GSANG RNAM DU 'KHOR GYI MNAL LTAS GONG GI DE DAG DANG CUNG ZAD MI 'DRA BA 'DI LTAR BYUNG STE,
rows.wylie: skabs 'dir rje rtogs ldan par mnal ltas byung tshul skor, mkhas grub thams cad mkhyen pas mdzad pa'i gsang rnam sogs su gong du bkod pa ltar byung zhing, rje blo gros legs bzang gis mdzad pa'i gsang rnam du 'khor gyi mnal ltas gong gi de dag dang cung zad mi 'dra ba 'di ltar byung ste
rows.english: Concerning the visions that Lord Tokdenpa experienced in his dreams at this point, works like the Secret Biography of the omniscient Kedrup Je give the account as we've presented it above.  We see though in the secret biography of Lord Lodru Leksang a slightly different version of the dream visions that Je Tsongkapa's disciples were experiencing during this period.

rows.acip: RJE 'DI PAS MA RGYUD PAI BSLAB BYA G-YON SKOR DANG PHYAG MDZAD PAR MOS PAS, DES 'DZUM PA DANG BCAS SNOD BCUD DE RJE 'DI'I SKU MDUN DU BTEG BYUNG BA DE LA MCHOD YAR ZHIG MDZAD NAS YAR CUNG ZAD CIG PHEBS TE,

rows.english: It occurred to our Lord that he should circle Her to the left, and throw himself down at her feet, as the rules of the Mother Tantra prescribe. rows.english: If we do come to understand just how to practice with this partner properly--if we know all the crucial points of the instructions for turning this practice into one for training the inner winds--then this is the highest method of all for making our journey along the spiritual path.  If though we make even just a slight error concerning these crucial points--or if any of the necessary steps or qualifications is missing in our practice--then it will cast us into the realms of hell, with no escape.  As such you must learn all these crucial points from the briefer, separate texts that have been written specifically upon this subject. * * * Gungtang Konchok Tenpay Drunme (1762-1823), an eminent Lama of the Gelukpa tradition, gives us some further qualifications that we might not remember to think about in His Light of the True Nature of the Teachings: An Extensive Commentary upon the "Very Meaningful Lines of Praise to Our Gentle Protector, the Buddha Himself Come Again, Based on a Description of the Way in which He Clarified the Very Essence of the Teachings" (ACIP digital text S0901, ff. 107a-107b):

rows.acip: DES NA GLANG PO CAN GYI RTZA'I MAR SNA NI, RTZA SNA GA-YON NAS GA-YAS SU CUNG ZAD 'KHYIL BA'I RNAM PAR YOD LA, DE'I RTAGS RTZA DE'I MAR SNA YOD PHYOGS KYI BUD MED DE'I SNA GA-YON NAS GA-YAS SU 'KHYIL BA'I RNAM PA CAN LA SOGS PA LAS, PHYAG RGYA DE GLANG PO CAN GYI RIGS SU GTOGS PA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: des na glang po can gyi rtsa'i mar sna ni, rtsa sna ga-yon nas ga-yas su cung zad 'khyil ba'i rnam par yod la, de'i rtags rtsa de'i mar sna yod phyogs kyi bud med de'i sna ga-yon nas ga-yas su 'khyil ba'i rnam pa can la sogs pa las, phyag rgya de glang po can gyi rigs su gtogs pa yin no
rows.english: And so let's talk first about the lower opening to the channel of a woman who is of the type called the "Lady of the Cow," or "Lady of the Elephant."  Here the opening of the channel turns a bit from left to the right; the indication that this is so is that this type of woman's opening--situated at the area of the lower end of the channel--also turns for example slightly from left to right.  When this is the case, then we classify this partner as belonging to the type of a "Lady of the Cow."

rows.acip: DE NAS RLUNG DBUS KYI THIG LE LA BSTIM LA, SHES PA'ANG DE NYID LA GTAD LA RLUNG KHA SBYAR TE, LAG PA GA-YON PAS LTE BA NYID DU MNAN, GA-YAS PAS PUS MO LA BSKOR BA LAN GCIG BYA, SE GOL GCIG GTOGS, DE NAS RLUNG PHYIR BTANG STE, DE LTA BU BRGYA LA SOGS PA BYED SNYING 'DOD TSAD BYAS LA THUN CHUNG DANG PO SONG BA DANG, CHANG LA SOGS PA KHA ZAS KYI BYA BA CUNG ZAD CIG BYAS LA, STAN LAS MI LDANG BAR NGAL BSO STE THUN CHUNG DANG PO'O,,
rows.wylie: de nas rlung dbus kyi thig le la bstim la, shes pa'ang de nyid la gtad la rlung kha sbyar te, lag pa ga-yon pas lte ba nyid du mnan, ga-yas pas pus mo la bskor ba lan gcig bya, se gol gcig gtogs, de nas rlung phyir btang ste, de lta bu brgya la sogs pa byed snying 'dod tshad byas la thun chung dang po song ba dang, chang la sogs pa kha zas kyi bya ba cung zad cig byas la, stan las mi ldang bar ngal bso ste thun chung dang po'o
rows.english: Next make the wind melt into the sphere at the middle, and focus your mind here as well.   Close the wind within a capsule.   With your left hand, press in at this same place, at the navel.   With your right hand, rub each knee with a circling gesture once, and then snap your fingers once.   After that, release the air.   Repeat this process a hundred times or something of the like, as much as you may desire.   This brings you to the end of your first short session.   Partake of some refreshment such as chang, resting yourself but not getting up off of your meditation cushion.   All this constitutes the first session.

rows.acip: RTZUB MO 'DI LA YANG BSKOR BA RE DANG SE GOL RE SPEL MAR BYAS NA CUNG ZAD 'JAM LA, BSKOR BA RNAMS PHYOGS GCIG, SE GOL RNAMS KYANG PHYOGS GCIG TU BYAS NA RTZUB BO,,
rows.wylie: rtsub mo 'di la yang bskor ba re dang se gol re spel mar byas na cung zad 'jam la, bskor ba rnams phyogs gcig, se gol rnams kyang phyogs gcig tu byas na rtsub bo
rows.english: This is the more drastic version of the practice; if you wish to do a more gentle one, then increase the rounds and corresponding fingersnaps only every other session.  There is also a drastic version where you do the rounds and the fingersnaps separately.

rows.acip: DE LA SPYI GTZUG GI HAm DANG, LTE BA'I AOm RTZA DBU MA KHA DOG DMAR PO SHIN TU CHA PHRA BA GCIG GIS ZUNG SBREL BAR BSGOM, RKANG PA GNYIS CUNG ZAD BSKYOD CING RLUNG BSKUMS PAS SEMS KYIS RKANG MTHIL DANG, 'OG SGO'I RLUNG GIS LTE BA'I AOm 'BAR,
rows.wylie: de la spyi gtsug gi haM dang, lte ba'i aoM rtsa dbu ma kha dog dmar po shin tu cha phra ba gcig gis zung sbrel bar bsgom, rkang pa gnyis cung zad bskyod cing rlung bskums pas sems kyis rkang mthil dang, 'og sgo'i rlung gis lte ba'i aoM 'bar
rows.english: Now go on and visualize the central channel as a very fine string, colored red and connecting the hang at the tip of your head to the om at your navel.  Move your two feet just a bit, and contract the winds.  Use your mind to get the winds at the soles of your feet, and the lower wind, to make the om at the navel blaze in flame.

rows.acip: STENG 'OG GI RLUNG KHA SBYAR, LUS CUNG ZAD BSGUL ZHING BSGOM, DES DROD LA SOGS PA HA CHANG CHE NAS DE BAS KLOD LA BSGOM, DE LTAR BSGOMS PAS DANG PO DROD 'BYUNG, DE NAS TSOR BA BDE BA SKYE, DE NAS MI RTOG PA'I BDE BA SKYE, DE NAS MTSON BYED DPE'I YE SHES RNAMS NYAMS SU MYONG BA SKYE,
rows.wylie: steng 'og gi rlung kha sbyar, lus cung zad bsgul zhing bsgom, des drod la sogs pa ha chang che nas de bas klod la bsgom, de ltar bsgoms pas dang po drod 'byung, de nas tshor ba bde ba skye, de nas mi rtog pa'i bde ba skye, de nas mtshon byed dpe'i ye shes rnams nyams su myong ba skye
rows.english: Now make a capsule of the upper and lower winds.  Let your body shake a little, a go into a meditation.  If the warmth and such produced by this meditation is too great, then loosen up the meditation. If you continue this meditation, then first you will get a sensation of warmth.  After that you will have a feeling of pleasure, and then non-conceptual bliss.  This then brings on experiences of what we call the "representative wisdom, the approximate wisdom."

rows.acip: MKHAL MA GNYIS DANG, RGYU ZHABS DANG, SNYING DANG, MGO NA KAM KAM PA BYUNG NA CUNG ZAD BCAG CING KHA ZAS BZA', DE NAS YANG BSGOM PAR BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: mkhal ma gnyis dang, rgyu zhabs dang, snying dang, mgo na kam kam pa byung na cung zad bcag cing kha zas bza', de nas yang bsgom par bya'o
rows.english: If you begin to feel a diffused pain throughout your two kidneys, or your lower intestines, or your heart or head, then break the meditation a bit and take some food.  Then go back and continue to meditate.

Then go back and continue to meditate."}

rows.acip: 'OG NA GNAS PA'I HIS YA BTEGS PA LA SOGS PA'I TSUL GYIS YAR PHUL TE, STENG GI KA LA SOGS PAS YAR DRANG ZHING, NGAG TU HI KA DRAG TU BRJOD, KA HI ZHES NGAL BSO ZHING SNYING GA'I BAR DU MAR 'ONG BAR BSMAS LA STENG RLUNG CUNG ZAD MNAN NO,,
rows.wylie: 'og na gnas pa'i his ya btegs pa la sogs pa'i tshul gyis yar phul te, steng gi ka la sogs pas yar drang zhing, ngag tu hi ka drag tu brjod, ka hi zhes ngal bso zhing snying ga'i bar du mar 'ong bar bsmas la steng rlung cung zad mnan no
rows.english: Then push everything up, using the hi at the bottom for example to push up against the ya.  Pull up the ka and the rest on the top, and in your words say hi ka very forcefuly.  Then say ka hi, which is meant to refresh you, and see everything coming back to the heart.  Press down a bit with the upper wind.

rows.acip: 'DA' KA MA'I GNAS 'DIS NI MTHO RIS ZHES BYA BA THAR PA'I GROGS SU 'GRO BA LAS, THAR PA KHO NA 'GRUB PA NI MA YIN ZHES GSUNGS NGO, ,TSE 'DI LA DBU MA CUNG ZAD KHA BYE BA RNAMS BAR DO NYID DU PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR BA YIN NO, GNAD KYI MAN NGAG LA BRTEN NAS RIM GYIS CHOS KYI DBYINGS RTOGS PA'I THABS BSTAN ZIN TO,,
rows.wylie: 'da' ka ma'i gnas 'dis ni mtho ris zhes bya ba thar pa'i grogs su 'gro ba las, thar pa kho na 'grub pa ni ma yin zhes gsungs ngo, ,tshe 'di la dbu ma cung zad kha bye ba rnams bar do nyid du phyag rgya chen po 'grub par 'gyur ba yin no, gnad kyi man ngag la brten nas rim gyis chos kyi dbyings rtogs pa'i thabs bstan zin to
rows.english: This crucial point, to be practiced at the moment of death, is said to refer to "higher births"; the idea being that it functions to aid you in reaching freedom, rather than leading itself to this goal.  Those who are able to open the central channel just a bit in this life achieve the realization of the great seal only during the inbetween state. This concludes our presentation of the method for perceiving ultimate reality through a successive process, by utilizing the advices on the crucial points.

rows.acip: 'DI YANG GZUGS CAN GYI RGYAN YIN LA, CUNG ZAD GO BDE BAR BRJOD NA, SPRIN DANG MKHYEN BRTZE SBYAR ZHING, 'GRO BA'I PHAN BDE NI KU MU DA'I TSAL DANG, CHOS BSTAN PA NI CHAR DANG SBYAR BA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: 'di yang gzugs can gyi rgyan yin la, cung zad go bde bar brjod na, sprin dang mkhyen brtse sbyar zhing, 'gro ba'i phan bde ni ku mu da'i tshal dang, chos bstan pa ni char dang sbyar ba yin no
rows.english: All of this is a physical metaphor; if we were to simplify it, we could say that the clouds relate to the knowledge and love of an Enlightened Being; that the garden of lilies represents benefit and happiness for all living beings; and that teaching the Dharma is the rain. A Supplication to Stay

A Supplication to Stay"}

rows.acip: GZUGS CAN GYI RGYAN YIN LA, DPE DON CUNG ZAD PHYE NA, 'KHOR BA NI, RGYA MTSO DANG SBYAR, LAS NYON GNYIS NI RBA KLONG DANG, SDUG BSNGAL GSUM NI CHU SRIN DANG 'KHOR BA 'DI TZAM NAS GTAN MED CES TSAD 'DZIN MI NUS NI, RGYA MTSO'I MTHA' DANG GTING PHAL PAS TSAD BZUNG MI NUS PA DANG SBYAR RO,,
rows.wylie: gzugs can gyi rgyan yin la, dpe don cung zad phye na, 'khor ba ni, rgya mtsho dang sbyar, las nyon gnyis ni rba klong dang, sdug bsngal gsum ni chu srin dang 'khor ba 'di tsam nas gtan med ces tshad 'dzin mi nus ni, rgya mtsho'i mtha' dang gting phal pas tshad bzung mi nus pa dang sbyar ro
rows.english: This is a case where we are using the simile of a physical object, and we can break out the elements of the metaphor as follows.  The cycle of pain is being compared to an ocean.  Karma and negative emotions are being compared to waves upon this sea, and the three types of suffering are sharks.  The cycle of pain itself is something whose extent cannot be defined: you cannot say that from this physical point on there is no touch of this cycle.  And this fact is being compared to the breadth and depth of the sea, whose extent cannot be grasped by any normal person.

rows.acip: ,DE BZHIN DU PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS NGA'O SNYAM PA 'BYUNG BA NA, PHUNG PO'I STENG NAS SNGA PHYI'I RGYUN GYI TSOGS PA DANG , DUS GCIG PA'I TSOGS PA DANG DE'I CHA SHAS DE'I MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU CUNG ZAD KYANG MED DE RGYAS PAR 'OG NAS 'CHAD DE,
rows.wylie: de bzhin du phung po la brten nas nga'o snyam pa 'byung ba na, phung po'i steng nas snga phyi'i rgyun gyi tshogs pa dang , dus gcig pa'i tshogs pa dang de'i cha shas de'i mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu cung zad kyang med de rgyas par 'og nas 'chad de
rows.english: The same thing happens when you get the idea of "me" about the heaps, the various components to yourself. There is nothing about these components as a whole, when you consider them as a continuum in time, nor as a whole considered in a single moment in time, nor as the various parts to a whole, that you could ever establish as being any kind of "me." We'll go into this in more detail further on.

rows.acip: DE BZHIN DU PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS NGA'O SNYAM PA 'BYUNG BA NA, PHUNG PO'I STENG NAS SNGA PHYI'I RGYUN GYI TSOGS PA DANG, DUS GCIG PA'I TSOGS PA DANG DE'I CHA SHAS DE'I MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU CUNG ZAD KYANG MED DE RGYAS PAR 'OG NAS 'CHAD DO,,
rows.wylie: de bzhin du phung po la brten nas nga'o snyam pa 'byung ba na, phung po'i steng nas snga phyi'i rgyun gyi tshogs pa dang, dus gcig pa'i tshogs pa dang de'i cha shas de'i mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu cung zad kyang med de rgyas par 'og nas 'chad do
rows.english: The same thing happens when we look at the parts of ourselves and think, “It's me.” At that point, there is not the slightest thing about these parts—neither in the collection of its earlier or later parts as it flows through time; nor in the collection of its parts considered in a single moment; nor in the individual parts themselves—which we could point to as being this “me.” We'll go into this in more detail below.
